script.title: Expenses under $75: do you still need the receipt?
script.hook: A common question: do I need a receipt for every small business expense?

segments.heading: Common question
segments.narration: A common question: do I need a receipt for every small business expense?
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. the small paper receipt mascot with a folded corner, round glasses and big eyes holding a tiny receipt. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: The rule
segments.narration: For travel, meals and gifts, the IRS generally doesn't require a receipt for an expense under seventy-five dollars. Lodging always needs one.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a coin with a small 75. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: But
segments.narration: You still need a record: the date, the amount, where, and the business purpose. A note in your log or on the card statement works.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a notebook with four lines. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Other costs
segments.narration: For other business costs, like supplies or software, keep proof of the payment and what it was for, whatever the amount.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a folder. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Sunday
segments.narration: Sunday's video covers every record worth keeping. Link in bio.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. the small paper receipt mascot with a folded corner, round glasses and big eyes waving. No text, no logos, no real people.

script.cta: Follow for one freelancer money move a week.
script.caption:
For travel, meal and gift expenses under $75 (other than lodging), the IRS generally doesn't require a receipt, but you still need a record of the date, amount, place and business purpose (Publication 463). Keep proof for other business costs.

Educational, not tax advice. 2026 federal figures; check your state.

Follow for one freelancer money move a week.
claims_to_verify: Pub 463: documentary evidence not needed for expenses under $75 except lodging; adequate records still required

script.title: 3 freelance records people toss too early
script.hook: Most tax records can go after about three years. Three kinds shouldn't.

segments.heading: Hook
segments.narration: Most tax records can go after about three years. Three kinds shouldn't.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. the small paper receipt mascot with a folded corner, round glasses and big eyes holding a folder close. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Number 3
segments.narration: Number three: receipts for equipment you're still using. Keep them until three years after the tax year you sell or get rid of it.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a laptop with a tag. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Number 2
segments.narration: Number two: anything showing income you left off. If you underreported by more than twenty-five percent, the IRS has six years.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a calendar with six pages. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Number 1
segments.narration: Number one: your filed returns. Keep copies indefinitely. They're the first thing a lender or the IRS asks about.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. a stack of forms. No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Sunday
segments.narration: The full keep-or-toss list is Sunday's video. Link in bio.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and warm paper cream with a coral accent and a mint highlight, simple shapes, paper texture. the small paper receipt mascot with a folded corner, round glasses and big eyes waving. No text, no logos, no real people.

script.cta: Follow for one freelancer money move a week.
script.caption:
Keep longer than three years: records for property and equipment (until the limitations period expires for the year you dispose of it), records for years where income was underreported by more than 25% (six years), and copies of filed returns (many people keep them indefinitely).

Educational, not tax advice. 2026 federal figures; check your state.

Follow for one freelancer money move a week.
claims_to_verify: IRS: 3 years general; 6 years if >25% income omitted; property records until limitations period expires for year of disposition
